questions.q: What is a standard candle in astronomy?
a: An astronomical object of known luminosity whose distance can be determined by measuring its apparent brightness
A star that burns hydrogen at a strictly constant temperature
A unit of stellar mass equal to our Sun
A hypothetical star used to calibrate telescope lenses

questions.q: What does Wien's displacement law state regarding the peak wavelength lambda_max of black-body radiation and its absolute temperature T?
a: lambda_max * T² = constant
lambda_max * T = constant (Wien's constant)
lambda_max = constant * T
lambda_max / T = constant

questions.q: What does Stefan-Boltzmann law state for the total radiant power (luminosity L) emitted by a spherical star of radius R and surface temperature T?
a: L = 4 * pi * R * sigma * T²
L = sigma * T⁴ / (4 * pi * R²)
L = 4 * pi * R² * sigma * T⁴
L = 4 / (pi * R² * sigma * T⁴)

questions.q: What is a light-year (ly) defined as?
a: The time it takes for light to travel from the Moon to Earth
The distance the Earth travels around the Sun in one year
The distance from the Earth to the nearest star
The distance that a photon in a vacuum travels in one Julian year (3.15 x 10⁷ seconds)

questions.q: How is the astronomical distance of a star determined using the stellar parallax method?
a: By measuring the apparent shift in position of the star against distant background stars when viewed from opposite points in Earth's orbit around the Sun
By analyzing the red shift of its emission spectrum
By measuring its apparent brightness and applying Stefan-Boltzmann law
By timing how long radio echoes take to bounce off its surface

questions.q: What is one parsec (pc) defined as?
a: The distance at which the mean radius of Earth's orbit subtends an angle of one arcsecond
The distance light travels in one second
The distance from Earth to the center of the Milky Way galaxy
The radius of the observable universe

questions.q: What is Hubble's law relating the recessional speed v of a distant galaxy to its distance d from Earth (where H_0 is the Hubble constant)?
a: v = H_0 * d²
v = d / H_0
v = H_0 * d
v = H_0 / d

questions.q: What does the cosmological red shift of light from distant galaxies indicate?
a: Galaxies are moving closer together
The universe is contracting uniformly
Stars are aging and cooling down
Space itself is expanding, stretching the wavelength of light as it travels towards us

questions.q: What is the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) radiation considered to be?
a: Leftover thermal black-body radiation from the hot, dense early stages of the Big Bang, now cooled to about 2.7 K
Radiation emitted by black holes in galactic centers
Radio interference caused by solar wind
Scattered light from nearby stars

questions.q: What does the cosmological principle assume about the universe on a large scale?
a: The universe has a distinct center and edge
The universe is homogeneous and isotropic on a large scale
The universe is static and unchanging over infinite time
Physical laws change depending on location in the universe

questions.q: What is the primary energy source powering main-sequence stars like our Sun?
a: Gravitational contraction and cooling
Chemical combustion of hydrogen and oxygen
Nuclear fusion of hydrogen nuclei into helium nuclei via the proton-proton chain
Radioactive decay of uranium

questions.q: What happens to a star with a mass similar to our Sun at the end of its main-sequence lifetime?
a: It immediately explodes into a supernova leaving a black hole
It collapses into a neutron star directly
It turns into a white dwarf without any preceding stage
It expands into a red giant, sheds its outer layers to form a planetary nebula, and leaves behind a dense white dwarf core

questions.q: What is the Chandrasekhar limit?
a: The maximum stable mass of a white dwarf star, approximately 1.44 solar masses, beyond which it will collapse and explode as a Type Ia supernova
The maximum mass of a main-sequence star before hydrogen fusion ceases
The temperature limit for core nuclear fusion
The maximum distance measurable by stellar parallax

questions.q: What is a neutron star?
a: A cloud of cool interstellar gas
An extremely dense stellar remnant composed almost entirely of neutrons, supported by neutron degeneracy pressure
A star made of protons and electrons only
A black hole event horizon

questions.q: What defines the event horizon of a black hole?
a: The physical solid surface of the collapsed star
The point where magnetic fields are strongest
The boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape due to gravitational pull
The outer radius where stellar wind stops

questions.q: What are Type Ia supernovae used for in cosmology?
a: To measure the rotational speed of nearby planets
To study solar flare activity
To measure atmospheric temperature on Earth
As standard candles to determine the distances of very distant galaxies and map the accelerated expansion of the universe

questions.q: What is stellar parallax angle p used to calculate distance d (in parsecs) to a nearby star?
a: d = 1 / p (where p is in arcseconds)
d = tan(p)

questions.q: What does the Doppler formula for red shift (delta lambda / lambda approx v / c) apply to in astronomy?
a: Expansion of space on cosmological scales
Determining the radial velocity v of stars or nearby galaxies moving through space relative to Earth
Calculating stellar surface temperatures
Measuring star radii via Stefan-Boltzmann law

questions.q: What is the approximate age of the universe estimated from the reciprocal of the Hubble constant (1 / H_0)?
a: 4.5 billion years
1 million years
Approximately 14 billion years
100 billion years

questions.q: What characteristic features appear in the absorption spectrum of a star's atmosphere?
a: Bright colored lines on a complete black background
Continuous rainbow spectrum without any interruptions
Completely black spectrum with zero light at all wavelengths
Dark absorption lines superimposed on a continuous spectrum, corresponding to specific photon frequencies absorbed by cooler outer gases

questions.q: How does the surface temperature of a star relate to its color?
a: Hotter stars appear blue or white, while cooler stars appear red or orange
Hotter stars appear deep red, while cooler stars appear bright blue
Star color depends entirely on distance from Earth, not temperature
All main-sequence stars are pure yellow

questions.q: What is the Hertzsprung-Russell (H-R) diagram?
a: A chart plotting star mass against star age
A scatter plot of stars showing the relationship between stellar luminosity (or absolute magnitude) and surface temperature (or spectral class)
A map of galaxy clusters across the observable universe
A graph of stellar magnetic field strength versus rotation period

questions.q: Where are most stars located on an H-R diagram during the majority of their active lifetimes?
a: The white dwarf cooling branch
The supergiant upper right corner
The main sequence running diagonally from hot, luminous blue stars to cool, dim red stars
The planetary nebula ring

questions.q: What causes the acceleration in the expansion of the universe discovered via distant Type Ia supernovae measurements?
a: Dark matter pulling galaxies apart
Solar radiation pressure from massive stars
Collisions between neighboring galaxy clusters
Dark energy acting as a repulsive force across cosmological scales

questions.q: What is dark matter?
a: Hypothetical non-luminous matter that does not emit, absorb, or reflect electromagnetic radiation, but whose presence is inferred from gravitational effects on galaxies
Dust clouds blocking starlight in the Milky Way
Dead black dwarf stars packed together
Interstellar magnetic fields

questions.q: What is the apparent magnitude m of a star a measure of?
a: Its intrinsic power output
How bright a star appears to an observer on Earth
Its physical diameter in kilometers
Its distance in parsecs

questions.q: What is the absolute magnitude M of a star defined as?
a: The brightness of the star viewed from the Sun
The total energy emitted per second
The apparent magnitude the star would have if it were placed at a standard distance of 10 parsecs (32.6 light-years)
The magnitude corrected for atmospheric extinction

questions.q: What is the distance modulus formula relating apparent magnitude m, absolute magnitude M, and distance d in parsecs?
a: m - M = 5 * log(d)
m - M = 5 * log(d) - 5
m + M = 5 * log(d) + 10

a: They contain fewer hydrogen atoms initially

a: r_s = G * M / c
r_s = 2 * G * M / c
